newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 30.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- AT&T will end 1996 with roughly the same number of employees as it started with, despite high-profile downsizing moves.
- Long Island Lighting agreed to merge with Brooklyn Union Gas in a stock swap valued at $3 billion.
- Write-offs taken in the early 1990s for items such as retirees' health care could be a hidden boon for some firms.
- The Dow Jones industrials rose 14.23 to a record 6560.91.
- Durable goods orders fell 1.6 percent in November.
- Western states accounted for most of the gain in holiday sales among major retailers.
- Nordstrom said same-store holiday sales "declined moderately" from a year ago and its quarterly profit won't meet analysts' expectations.
- Marvel Entertainment filed for bankruptcy court protection.
- The dollar's rise against the yen is making the U.S. a less attractive place for Japanese manufacturers to produce their goods.
- Big law firms are expecting 1996 to be a second consecutive strong year for profits, fueled in part by a boom in mergers and acquisitions.
- Viacom's Blockbuster is launching an ad campaign stressing its move into compact disks, CD-ROMs, magazines and other items.
- Sega said it expects fiscal 1997 profit to be 47 percent lower than its earlier projection.
- Computer Associates stock fell 21 percent after the company announced that its quarterly sales won't meet analysts' estimates.
- Chrysler said it is boosting the prices of some 1997 minivans, pickups and cars by $30 to $405 a vehicle.
- The $574 million issue of so-called Baby Berkshire Class B shares aimed at smaller investors "has been one of the real dogs of the year."
- A new class of foreign securities is starting to gain attention from investors of all stripes: post emerging markets bonds.
